label: first copy-phase step after re-reading a leading z (L>=4)
explanation: Fires at step t = L+1, the step right after <DEL>. There the model has fed back its first output and is emitting original token 1. The feature fires when that fed-back input is z, meaning the sequence started with z. This holds 97% of activation mass with precision 1.0 on dev. Every top example (about 0.95-1.0 of max) is z ... <DEL> z, mostly with L=6-8. Some z-start sequences reach only about 0.3-0.6 of max, so magnitude varies with context, but I did not isolate what drives it. It is silent for L=3 (z-start sequences of length 3 are the only false positives). About a third of active steps are missed, but they carry only 3% of mass: very weak blips (<0.05 of max) at the same step with other first tokens, plus a few at recall_idx 2. It does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, or on z inputs at other positions.

issues: Checks pass. On test, the predicate has precision 1.0 (0 false positives in 16303 predicted steps) and mass recall 0.971. In the dev profile, the copy phase holds 100% of mass and recall_idx 1 holds 99.2%. in_tok z holds 97.8% of mass, and there is no meaningful activation in the original or delimiter phases (37 tiny blips at orig_idx 7-8).

Misses on test are all weak, under about 0.13 of max: 8115 steps holding 2.9% of mass. They sit at step L+1 and are spread across non-z first tokens, plus some recall_idx 2 steps. They read as scattered noise, not a systematic class.

The magnitude driver the explanation left open is mostly sequence length. Mean activation per predicate step (mass share / count) for L=4 is about half that of L>=5: 0.075/2451 vs 0.153/2704, and about 0.18-0.19/2750 for L=6-9. This likely accounts for the reported 0.3-0.6-of-max z-start cases. Activation grows with L and saturates around L>=6. It is a minor omission, not a refutation.
Minor overclaim: L=3 is not fully silent. The z-start L=3 predicate is 11% precise (47 of 419 steps fire), with negligible mass of 0.00015. 'Nearly silent' would be accurate.

The next output token does not systematically drive magnitude. Digit outputs and repeated-token sequences carry mass roughly in proportion to their counts. out_tok == z is somewhat weaker (0.032 of mass over 492 steps).
